smart_decode_error: Smart decode: no known encoding detected in this panel.
guide_intro: Works like Burp's Decoder: each row is a panel holding some text. Transform it and the result appears as a new panel below, so you can keep chaining: decode base64, then URL, then hash it, all in one stack.
guide_step1_title: Paste text into the first panel
guide_step1_body: The top panel is your input: type or paste anything into it.
guide_step2_title: Pick a transform from a panel's dropdowns
guide_step2_body: <0>Decode as…</0> and <1>Encode as…</1> cover Base64 (standard and URL-safe), Base32, Hex, URL percent-encoding, HTML entities and Gzip (shown as base64, since compressed bytes aren't printable text). <2>Hash…</2> runs MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512, which are one-way, so there's no decode side for those.
guide_step3_title: Not sure what it is? Click "Smart decode"
guide_step3_body: It detects the encoding automatically (HTML entities, %-encoding, Base64/32, hex, gzip) and peels off as many layers as it can find in one click, adding one panel per layer.
guide_step4_title: Edit any panel, or use Text/Hex to inspect bytes
guide_step4_body: Editing a panel's content drops every panel after it, since they'd otherwise be showing a stale result. The Text/Hex toggle switches a panel between its plain-text view and a hex dump of the underlying bytes, handy after a gzip decode or anything non-printable.
guide_footer_note: Everything here runs locally against the text you provide: no requests are made to any target.
